newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - April 8.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said after a meeting yesterday with Wu Bangguo, vice-chairman of the Chinese cabinet, that the Chinese side will soon take up the issue of two blocks of heating power plants in China, which Czech businesses are interested in.
- Eleven members of the association of major drug distributors (Avel) authorised Pavel Suchy, Petr Himl and Tomas Sokol to meet with Health Minister Jan Strasky about covering distributors' debts.
- Shareholders of Skoda Plzen will approve an increase in basic capital from 9.5 billion crowns currently to nearly 12 billion crowns on May 9.
- The chairman of the Social Democratic Party, Milos Zeman, criticised Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy for not keeping his promise on construction of the nuclear power plant Temelin.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny confirmed that the winner of the tender for building a military staff information system is EDS-Digital, despite protests from Unisys and IBM.

- Beginning this summer, Czech Airlines (CSA) and Air Ostrava will have joint flights 11 times weekly from Prague to Berlin and six times weekly from Prague to Kosic. This is according to a contract the airlines will sign today.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Nova Hut and Vitkovice are preparing restructuring which will include laying off workers. Vitkovice will lay off about 1,000 workers, and Nova Hut will lay off about 710 workers.

- Aside from two compulsory administrations, the Finance Ministry issued 28 fines on capital market participants in March worth a total of 5.15 million crowns, primarily for not fulfilling information requirements.

- According to a report published yesterday from the Czech National Bank, total foreign exchange reserves amounted to 15.144 billion dollars, 435.9 billion crowns at the end of this February. This is a month-on-month increase of 14.2 billion crowns.

- More than 10 foreign investors are interested in privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB). Within less than two weeks, these investors should specify their preliminary intentions and show how the bank would operate if their offers win the tender for a 31.5 percent stake.

PRAVO - Greece supports giving the Czech Republic membership in NATO and the EU. Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos announced this after a meeting in Prague yesterday with Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec.
- Motoinvest Group finished selling First CS Holding (formerly Creditanstalt, Czech Investment Fund) and CS Investment Infrastructural Fund (formerly Creditanstalt, Czech Investment Fund).

- A "package of measures" which the cabinet decided to take in order to stabilise the macroeconomic situation, will most probably also concern import surcharges, according to an analyst from Patria Finance, Petr Zahradnicek.
